nodes.label: Supply chain transparency

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_000
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What is the common definition of transparency in the context of value chains, and what does it entail?
nodes.answer: Transparency is commonly defined as the relevant information being made available to all elements of the value chain in a harmonized way, allowing for common understanding, accessibility, clarity, and comparison.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_001
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What is the importance of supply chain collaboration for transparency in the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: Supply chain collaboration is crucial for transparency in the fashion industry as it helps businesses track and trace the journey of their products, ensuring ethical practices and sustainability throughout the supply chain.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_002
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why is the progress towards greater transparency in the fashion industry still slow?
nodes.answer: The progress towards greater transparency in the fashion industry is slow because many brands are lagging behind, communicating covertly, and not sharing much relevant business and supply chain information.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is achieving transparency in the fashion industry challenging for some brands?
nodes.answer: Achieving transparency in the fashion industry can be challenging for some brands, especially when they do not track their entire supply chain. This can result in limited traceability and missing supply chain data, making it difficult to achieve greater transparency.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did the Fashion Transparency Index reveal the selective disclosure practices of fashion brands during the pandemic?
nodes.answer: The Fashion Transparency Index (FTI) 2021 revealed that only 3% of 250 fashion brands formally disclosed on their websites the percentage of supply chain workers who lost jobs due to the pandemic turmoil, indicating selective disclosure practices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_005
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why is it challenging to access accurate data related to fashion supply chain impacts?
nodes.answer: The fragmented structure of fashion supply chains makes it difficult to access accurate data as outside impacts are not directly under corporate control, leading to only partially correct disclosure of supply chain impacts.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_006
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are some predominant regulatory responses aimed at mandating greater transparency in the fashion supply chain?
nodes.answer: The California Transparency in Supply Chain Acts, the UK Modern Slavery Act, and the Registration, Evaluation, Authorization of Chemicals (REACH) are some predominant regulatory responses created to mandate greater transparency in the fashion supply chain.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_007
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How do luxury brands differ from mass-market brands in terms of supply chain transparency?
nodes.answer: Luxury brands are often more secretive about their production practices to protect their expertise and maintain brand exclusivity, while mass-market brands heavily promote their supply chain commitments to enhance brand credibility.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why have luxury brands been secretive about their supply chain practices according to some studies?
nodes.answer: Luxury brands have been secretive about their supply chain practices mainly to maintain exclusivity, as argued by studies conducted by Stable and Merz (2017) and Marksman et al. (2017).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: According to Jestratijevic et al. (2020), what was the probability that a mass-market brand had a higher transparency score in the supply chain area compared to a luxury brand in 2017?
nodes.answer: Jestratijevic et al. (2020) found that the probability that a mass-market brand had a higher transparency score than a luxury brand in the supply chain area was 76% in 2017.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_010
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are the two main categories that the Fashion Transparency Index data covers?
nodes.answer: The Fashion Transparency Index data covers corporate transparency related to policies and governance, as well as supply chain transparency related to traceability, audits, and negative impact reporting.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_011
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the three major trends identified in the data regarding brand transparency?
nodes.answer: The three major trends identified in the data are progress towards greater transparency, selective disclosure of corporate information over supply chain information, and mass-market fashion brands being more transparent than luxury brands in supply chain disclosures.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_012
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What type of information did brands disclose more of according to the results?
nodes.answer: Brands disclosed more information about corporate transparency than supply chain transparency at a rate that was largely unchanged over time.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_013
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How have the transparency levels of mass-market fashion brands and luxury brands' supply chains changed over time?
nodes.answer: The gap between the transparency of supply chains of mass-market fashion brands and luxury brands has narrowed.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_014
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which model showed a better fit for most areas of supply chain transparency analysis, and which model was better for negative impact reporting?
nodes.answer: The varying-gap model was the better fitting model for most areas of supply chain transparency analysis, except for negative impact reporting, where the constant-gap model had the better fit.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_015
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How has the gap between mass-market and luxury brands on overall supply chain transparency evolved over time?
nodes.answer: The gap between mass-market and luxury brands on overall supply chain transparency increased slightly until 2,020 after which it narrowed. By 2,023 the gap was no longer statistically significant.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_016
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: In which specific area did the gap between mass-market and luxury brands on supply chain transparency not show statistical significance from 2022 onwards?
nodes.answer: In the audit area, from 2022 onwards, the gap between mass-market and luxury brands was not statistically significant.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Ethical sourcing standards|Supply chain transparency_qna_017
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What potential benefits can Open Data Standards efforts bring to supply chain reporting standards?
nodes.answer: Open Data Standards efforts may increase transparency and reduce opacity in supply chain reporting standards, leading to improved accuracy and reliability in reporting.
